methodological_questions: How to define PNR fail from play-by-play data (e.g., no score, turnover, missed shot)?

historical_evidence.finding: Within-game adapter PPP improvement of +0.058 was later deemed an artifact driven by selection on extreme early-third PPP causing mean reversion (no_signal baseline +0.126 outperformed adapters).

evidence_establishes: Earlier within-game counter/adaptation studies (SF13, SF12, SF-APPA-001) using PPP deltas and play-type share shifts consistently suffered from regression-to-the-mean artifacts and were either artifacts or inconclusive.

evidence_does_not_establish: Whether pull-up shots after a failed PNR show a league-wide lift of >0 in ≥70% of defensive units with median >2pp.
The appropriate baseline for measuring lift on such counter possessions.
The sample size available per defensive unit for this rare event sequence.
The stability of unit-level median lift estimates with realistic event counts.
own_inferences: The question can be operationally defined using PBP action types and possession data, but the rare nature of PNR-fail → pull-up sequences will severely limit per-unit sample size.
If 'defensive unit' is team-season (30 teams), each unit may have 50–150 such possessions across a season, making a 2pp median difference potentially detectable but with wide uncertainty.
The primary inferential threat is regression to the mean, because a PNR-fail is defined by a negative offensive outcome; subsequent possessions may naturally regress upward, mimicking a counter lift.
Without a carefully defined baseline (e.g., pull-up PPP against the same defense in other situations, matched on game state), any positive lift could be an artifact.
A falsification test using non-pull-up shot types after PNR-fail or pull-ups after non-fail PNR would strengthen causal interpretation.
uncertainties: Exact count of PNR-fail → pull-up possessions per defensive unit across the available seasons.
Whether the bulk of PNR-fail events result in a change of possession before the pull-up, affecting the counter timing.
The true effect size, if any, and whether it exceeds the noise floor of 2pp.
Optimal unit definition (team, team-season, defensive lineup) given the trade-off between sample size and relevance to the league-wide claim.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the historical evidence, the approach might have directly used early-game PPP baselines or adaptive-play-type share methods similar to SF13. blocking_constraints.text: Expected number of PNR-fail followed by pull-up possessions per defensive unit is likely moderate, making the 2pp lift requirement underpowered for many units.
PNR fails are a small fraction of all possessions; subsequent pull-up shots are rarer; many units may have zero or very few events, compromising the >=70% test and median.
A PNR-fail is defined by a bad offensive outcome; any comparison with a broader possession or shot-type baseline risks inflating lift via regression to the mean, as seen in SF13 and SF-APPA-001.

prior_work.summary: Previous counter-adaptation studies (SF13, SF12, SF-APPA-001) found either artifacts or inconclusive results due to regression to the mean and selection flaws. No direct test of the PNR-fail → pull-up counter has been conducted, but the methodological pitfalls are well-characterized.

risks.text: Lift computed on PNR-fail pull-up possessions vs a stable baseline may over-estimate from mean reversion because the PNR-fail sample is selected on a negative outcome.
Per-unit counts of PNR-fail-pull-up events could be too small to reliably test median >2pp and 70% sign criterion.
Many defensive units may have zero or very few relevant possessions, making the proportion of units with positive lift unstable.
Game situation (score, clock, period) and player skill influence both the decision to pull-up and the shot outcome, potentially creating a spurious correlation with the preceding PNR-fail.
Uncertainty in reliably identifying PNR failure from PBP action types and linking to a subsequent pull-up as an intentional counter (versus a forced shot).
If multiple unit definitions are explored, the proportion-of-units test inflates false positive rate unless pre-specified.

design.estimand: For each defensive unit (team-season), the difference between points per possession on possessions where the offense attempts a pull-up field goal after a failed pick-and-roll against that unit and the same offense's pull-up PPP against that unit in other possessions matched on score margin, period, and shot-clock quartile.
design.unit: Defensive team-season (e.g., the Boston Celtics' regular season 2022-23). Sensitivity: also consider team across all seasons.
design.sample: All regular season and playoff games from NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26, excluding the partial 2025-26 data flagged as incomplete. PNR-fail events defined from PBP: the possession ends with no points (turnover, defensive rebound, shot clock violation) after a pick-and-roll action. The next offensive possession (or an immediate offensive rebound that leads to a pull-up) is the counter observation.
design.power: Power analysis to be performed before extraction: estimate per-team-season event count from pilot 2024-25 data. Provide 80% power for a one-sided rank test that the median lift >2pp and for the sign test that >70% of units show positive lift, assuming true effect of 4pp and expected per-unit sample ~80 events. If pilot shows inadequate counts, pool multiple seasons per team.
design.controls: Baseline pull-up PPP matched on: score margin (leading/trailing/tied), period, and shot-clock remaining (bin by 24-18, 17-10, 9-4, <4 seconds). Exclude garbage time (score margin >20 in 4th quarter). Remove possessions where the pull-up follows a PNR-fail but with an intervening dead ball or full change of possession (e.g., defensive rebound and then offensive possession at other end).
design.falsification: 1) Compute lift for non-pull-up shot types (catch-and-shoot, drives) after a PNR-fail; the pull-up lift should be larger. 2) Compute lift on pull-ups after successful PNR (scored or drew foul); this should not show systematic positive lift relative to baseline. 3) Permute the PNR outcome labels within each unit and recompute the unit-level median; the observed median should be in the upper tail of the null distribution.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify the primary unit as defensive team-season. Only one aggregate test: proportion of units with lift>0 and median lift>2pp. No subgroup or multiple unit definitions without Bonferroni correction. Report all pre-registered falsification tests without multiplicity adjustment.
design.decision_rule: The counter hypothesis is supported if: (a) ≥70% of defensive team-season units have estimated lift > 0, (b) the median of the unit lifts is > 2 pp, and (c) the falsification checks show the pull-up lift exceeds non-pull-up lift and pull-ups after successful PNR, and the permutation test results in p < 0.05 (one-sided).

What sample sizes are needed for unit-level median lift?
